A person from North America (Canada) spent 9 years in the UK and is currently living in a Southeast Asian country for 5 years, with extensive travel experience overseas.

- There's more than one way to do things, and other ways aren't wrong. They're just different.
- There's more than one way to say things too, and that's ok. Courgette, zucchini. Eggplant, aubergine. Just add some new vocabulary to your list and understand both. Move on.
- Everyone should travel for these reasons alone - to realize that their way is not the only way. It's extremely ignorant to think you're the only right one.
- English is a difficult and confusing language to learn.
- I am very lucky. Very lucky, to have the opportunities I've had. In my travels in the developing world, I've met so many people that have so little, and are no less deserving than me.
- There are good people everywhere.
- There are bad people everywhere.
- North Americans can be very wasteful with food and things we buy.
- We are more environmentally conscious in other ways though (recycling, etc)!
- We are VERY consumeristic.
- North Americans can be very work-focused and money-driven.
- Other cultures have a way more relaxed, laid-back, and enjoy life approach.

TL;DR: different is ok.
